answers: At 1e16 W: holding a 1e6 kg sail at 0.1 g needs P = m a c/2 x (1+b)/(1-b) = 1.5e14 W at rest, 1.8e14 W at 0.1c, for ~1 yr (0.1 g x 1 yr = 0.1c). So ~55 sails can be driven concurrently: ~50 seeds/yr. A phased array can retarget between sails only while they sit inside its diffraction range (2.44 lambda L/D = 37 km spot at 0.05 ly for 30 km), which is the whole ~1 yr acceleration run, so time-sharing buys nothing beyond the power limit.

Pollutants at 10-50 kly: in-plane A_V is ~10-50 mag at V but ~1-5 at 10 um, so mid-IR only. Resolving the planet needs a baseline >= lambda*d/1 AU = 630 m at 10 kly and 3.2 km at 50 kly (your 2 AU aperture is far beyond that). Photons: an Earth analogue's 10 um flux at 10 kly is ~1e-25 W/m2; a 1e-3-deep band at S/N 10 needs ~1e8 photons, i.e. ~1e10 m2 for ~1e5 s before extinction, x10-100 after it. Each target is cheap for 1e16 m2 of film; the limit is survey rate (~1e4-1e5 targets per day) and sightlines with A_V<5.
